prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: EN · Issue tracker (language en).
Grid: 6 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "ID" · longest unbreakable word 39px · one-line width 75px
  col 2: header "Title" · longest unbreakable word 92px · one-line width 394px
  col 3: header "Severity" · longest unbreakable word 59px · one-line width 59px
  col 4: header "Assignee" · longest unbreakable word 66px · one-line width 66px
  col 5: header "Status" · longest unbreakable word 61px · one-line width 77px
  col 6: header "Updated" · longest unbreakable word 62px · one-line width 87px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A phone-width issue tracker for scanning and triaging bugs: identify the issue, judge urgency/status, see ownership and recency.","reading":"Readers scan top-down by row: ID and title locate the issue, then severity/status/assignee/updated answer triage questions. Cross-row comparison is mainly severity, status and recency.","groups":["ID + Title: together form the row identity and the primary scan path","Severity + Status: both express triage state and are compared across rows","Assignee + Updated: secondary ownership and recency metadata, read after triage state"],"keep_intact":["ID strings such as BUG-2041, including the hyphen","Severity and status values and their headers","Assignee names","Updated dates or relative times"],"may_wrap":["Title at word boundaries","Headers when space is tight","Two-word status or updated values at spaces, not inside words","Assignee names at spaces"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[96,119,36,36,36,36],"idea":"Single-screen compromise: keep every column visible and IDs intact, but let title and metadata wrap or split heavily."},{"name":"B","widths":[96,160,80,87,82,83],"idea":"Moderate horizontal scroll: title wraps naturally while every metadata column has room for its longest word, keeping triage values intact."},{"name":"C","widths":[96,415,80,87,98,108],"idea":"One-line ledger: use each column's natural one-line width, accepting a very wide horizontal scroll in exchange for no wrapping or splitting."}]}
